title: Pasta e Fagioli
subtitle: Thick Italian bean and pasta soup
excerpt: A thick Neapolitan soup of borlotti beans and short pasta in a tomato-rosemary broth. Half the beans are mashed to give the dish its characteristic dense, creamy texture. Peasant food in the best sense.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pasta e fagioli is one of the great dishes of the cucina povera tradition, peasant cooking that uses dried beans and simple pasta to create something deeply satisfying from minimal ingredients. Every region of Italy has a version. The Neapolitan version includes tomato and rosemary; the Venetian version uses borlotti beans and is served almost dry; the Roman version often includes pancetta. This recipe is in the southern Italian tradition.

content.text: The texture of pasta e fagioli comes from mashing or blending roughly half the beans before adding the pasta. This turns the broth into a thick, creamy base. It should sit on the boundary between soup and stew, not a clear broth with beans floating in it, but something so thick you can barely pour it. Use tinned borlotti if you can find them; cannellini are a fine substitute.

items.preparation: grated, plus a rind if available

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, celery, and carrot for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and half the beans. Pour in the stock and add the parmesan rind if using. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the rosemary sprigs and parmesan rind. Use a potato masher or blender to roughly puree about half the soup, leave it chunky. Add the remaining whole beans and return to a simmer.

Add the pasta and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often as it will catch on the bottom, until tender. The soup should be very thick. Add a splash more stock if needed. Serve with grated parmesan and a good drizzle of olive oil.
